nodes.name: Long-time behavior of the Einstein and Einstein-$\La$ flow on closed spatial manifolds
nodes.statement: A fundamental open problem in the mathematical study of cosmological models is the determination of the long-time behavior of the Einstein flow ($\La=0$) or the Einstein-$\La$ flow ($\La>0$) on closed spatial manifolds $M$, where $\La$ denotes the cosmological constant.
nodes.statement_short: Determining the long-time behavior of the Einstein ($\La=0$) and Einstein-$\La$ ($\La>0$) flows on closed spatial manifolds is open.

nodes.name: Einstein flow
nodes.statement: By \emph{Einstein flow} we refer to the form of the Einstein equations when a foliation of spacetime is chosen. In that case the equations appear as a system of PDEs that determines the evolution of geometric tensor fields and is in this way similar to other geometric flows.
nodes.origin_citation: term coined in earlier works; cf. Andersson & Moncrief 2011
nodes.genus: the form of the Einstein equations
differentia: when a foliation of spacetime is chosen
the equations appear as a system of PDEs that determines the evolution of geometric tensor fields

nodes.name: Closed Universe Recollapse conjecture
nodes.statement: If $M$ is three-dimensional and of positive Yamabe type $Y_+$, it is conjectured that its maximal globally hyperbolic development (MGHD) recollapses, i.e.~is future and past geodesically incomplete \cite{BaGaTi86} (\emph{Closed Universe Recollapse conjecture}).
nodes.statement_short: Closed 3-manifolds of positive Yamabe type are conjectured to have recollapsing maximal globally hyperbolic developments.
assumptions: $M$ is three-dimensional and of positive Yamabe type $Y_+$
conclusions: its maximal globally hyperbolic development (MGHD) recollapses, i.e.~is future and past geodesically incomplete

nodes.name: Recollapse for spherically symmetric solutions
nodes.statement: This behavior is proven for the class of spherically symmetric solutions \cite{BuRe96,He02}.
nodes.statement_short: The closed-universe recollapse behavior is established for spherically symmetric solutions.
assumptions: $M$ is three-dimensional and of positive Yamabe type $Y_+$
the class of spherically symmetric solutions
conclusions: This behavior is proven for the class of spherically symmetric solutions

nodes.name: Milne model as an attractor of the Einstein flow
nodes.statement: In the negative Yamabe class $Y_-$ it is known that in an open neighborhood of initial data corresponding to the Milne model, this solution serves as an attractor of the Einstein flow \cite{AnMo11}.
nodes.statement_short: In the $Y_-$ class the Milne model attracts the Einstein flow for nearby initial data.
assumptions: In the negative Yamabe class $Y_-$
in an open neighborhood of initial data corresponding to the Milne model
conclusions: this solution serves as an attractor of the Einstein flow

nodes.name: Prototypicality of the Milne model in the classes $Y_-$ and $Y_0$
nodes.statement: It is conjectured that under additional restrictions the global geometry of the Milne model (future completeness) is prototypical for the behavior of the Einstein flow in the classes $Y_-$ or $Y_0$ (but the spacetime has to be non-flat) in three spatial dimensions, i.e.~that the spacetimes admit CMC foliations where the mean curvature takes values in $(-\infty,0)$ and that this foliation covers the entire spacetime \cite{Re96}.
nodes.statement_short: Conjecture that future-complete Milne-like behavior with global CMC foliations is typical in the $Y_-$ and $Y_0$ classes in three spatial dimensions.
assumptions: under additional restrictions
(but the spacetime has to be non-flat) in three spatial dimensions
conclusions: the global geometry of the Milne model (future completeness) is prototypical for the behavior of the Einstein flow in the classes $Y_-$ or $Y_0$ (but the spacetime has to be non-flat) in three spatial dimensions
the spacetimes admit CMC foliations where the mean curvature takes values in $(-\infty,0)$ and that this foliation covers the entire spacetime

nodes.name: Future nonlinear stability of homogeneous models with $\La>0$
nodes.statement: All those models are future nonlinear stable \cite{Ri08}.
nodes.statement_short: The homogeneous $\La>0$ models with non-positive Yamabe Cauchy surfaces are nonlinearly stable towards the future.
assumptions: For Cauchy hypersurfaces in the negative or zero Yamabe class homogeneous models are past incomplete and future complete
conclusions: All those models are future nonlinear stable

nodes.name: Initial data for product spacetimes
nodes.statement: Initial data for spacetimes of this form at $t=0$ is given by $(M_1\times M_2,\la_1,\la_2,\dot x(0),\dot y (0))$. We assume $x(0)=y(0)=0$ without loss of generality. Note that other values for $x$ and $y$ can be encoded in the constants $\la_1$ and $\la_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Initial data is the tuple $(M_1\times M_2,\la_1,\la_2,\dot x(0),\dot y(0))$, normalized by $x(0)=y(0)=0$.

nodes.name: Trichotomy for product models with $n(n-1)=n_1\la_1+n_2\la_2$
nodes.statement: Let $\Lambda=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$ and let $M_1$, $M_2$ be closed manifolds of dimension $\dim M_i=n_i\geq 2$, $n_1+n_2=n$. Consider initial data of the form $x(0)=y(0)=\dot x(0)=\dot y(0)=0$ such that \eq{ n(n-1)=n_1\la_1+n_2\la_2, } holds. Then the following cases occur. \begin{enumerate} \item If $\la_2>n$ and $\la_1<(n_1-1)n/n_1$, the MGHD recollapses, i.e.~is future- and past incomplete, $I=(t_-,t_+)$ for $t_-<0<t_+$. Both singularities are of Kasner-type, i.e.~one factor collapses and the other factor has unbounded volume as $t\rightarrow t_{\pm}$. The mean curvature $H\rightarrow \pm\infty$ as $t\rightarrow t_{\pm}$. The Kretschmann scalar is unbounded towards both singularities. In particular, the MGHDs are $C^2$-inextendible. \item If $\la_2=n$ and $\la_1=(n_1-1)n/n_1$, MGHD is \eq{ \left(\mathbb R\times M_1\times M_2,-dt^2+\cosh\left(\sqrt{\frac{n}{n_1}}t\right)^2\cdot g_1 + g_2\right), } and in particular future and past complete. \item If $n(n_1-1)/n_1<\la_1<(n-1)$ or equivalently $n-1<\la_2<n$ the MGHD is future- and past complete. In both time directions, both factors expand exponentially with asymptotic growth rates depending only on the dimensions $n_1$ and $n_2$. \end{enumerate} Furthermore, the behavior is stable in the following sense. Initial data induced by any recollapsing solution in the class above has an open\footnote{Here, open is meant in the sense of $(g,K)\in H^\ell\times H^{\ell-1}$ spaces with $\ell=\ell(n)$ sufficiently large, where $(g,K)$ denote the spatial metric and second fundamental form, respectively.} neighborhood in the initial-data manifold, such that the MGHD of each element in this neighborhood recollapses. Similarly, initial data induced by any complete solution (except the critical solution) has an open neighborhood with elements that give rise to complete MGHDs. The critical solution \eqref{crit-sol} is unstable.
nodes.statement_short: For $\Lambda=n(n-1)/2$ on $M_1\times M_2$, curvature disequilibrium gives recollapsing MGHDs, the critical case gives an unstable complete solution, and near-equilibrium data give stable future- and past-complete MGHDs.
assumptions: $\Lambda=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$
$M_1$, $M_2$ be closed manifolds of dimension $\dim M_i=n_i\geq 2$, $n_1+n_2=n$
initial data of the form $x(0)=y(0)=\dot x(0)=\dot y(0)=0$
conclusions: If $\la_2>n$ and $\la_1<(n_1-1)n/n_1$, the MGHD recollapses, i.e.~is future- and past incomplete, $I=(t_-,t_+)$ for $t_-<0<t_+$. Both singularities are of Kasner-type, i.e.~one factor collapses and the other factor has unbounded volume as $t\rightarrow t_{\pm}$. The mean curvature $H\rightarrow \pm\infty$ as $t\rightarrow t_{\pm}$. The Kretschmann scalar is unbounded towards both singularities. In particular, the MGHDs are $C^2$-inextendible.

If $\la_2=n$ and $\la_1=(n_1-1)n/n_1$, MGHD is \eq{ \left(\mathbb R\times M_1\times M_2,-dt^2+\cosh\left(\sqrt{\frac{n}{n_1}}t\right)^2\cdot g_1 + g_2\right), } and in particular future and past complete.

If $n(n_1-1)/n_1<\la_1<(n-1)$ or equivalently $n-1<\la_2<n$ the MGHD is future- and past complete. In both time directions, both factors expand exponentially with asymptotic growth rates depending only on the dimensions $n_1$ and $n_2$.

Furthermore, the behavior is stable in the following sense. Initial data induced by any recollapsing solution in the class above has an open\footnote{Here, open is meant in the sense of $(g,K)\in H^\ell\times H^{\ell-1}$ spaces with $\ell=\ell(n)$ sufficiently large, where $(g,K)$ denote the spatial metric and second fundamental form, respectively.} neighborhood in the initial-data manifold, such that the MGHD of each element in this neighborhood recollapses. Similarly, initial data induced by any complete solution (except the critical solution) has an open neighborhood with elements that give rise to complete MGHDs. The critical solution \eqref{crit-sol} is unstable.

nodes.name: The background solution $\la_1=\la_2=n-1$ and the symmetric subcases
nodes.statement: The case $\la_1=\la_2=n-1$ corresponds to the background solution \eq{ -dt^2+ \cosh(t)^2 \cdot (g_1+g_2). } If $\la_2<\la_1$ we divide into three subcases that relate to the previous cases by interchanging $\la_1$ and $\la_2$ (and $n_1$ and $n_2$) in the statements of the theorem.

nodes.name: Curvature disequilibrium as the criterion for recollapse
nodes.statement: Relation \eqref{eq-def-rel} provides a simple interpretation for the case $\la_1,\la_2>0$. Then the first condition in the theorem concerns initial data for which the curvatures of both factors differ substantially while the last condition corresponds to initial data where both factors are of equal or almost equal Ricci-curvature. We conclude that for the case of positive curvature recollapse corresponds to a disequilibrium in curvature between the factors.
nodes.statement_short: For positive $\la_1,\la_2$ the recollapse condition means the two factors have strongly differing Ricci curvature.

nodes.name: Product models with non-positive Einstein constants
nodes.statement: Every spacetime of the form \eqref{ansatz} with $\la_1,\la_2\leq 0$ is complete in one time direction and incomplete in the other.
assumptions: Every spacetime of the form \eqref{ansatz} with $\la_1,\la_2\leq 0$
conclusions: is complete in one time direction and incomplete in the other

nodes.name: Positive curvature is necessary for recollapse
nodes.statement: The previous theorem implies that within the class given by \eqref{ansatz} positive curvature of at least one factor is a necessary criterion for recollapse.

nodes.name: Nariai solution
nodes.statement: \eq{ -dt^2+\frac{1}{3}g_{\mathbb S^2}+\cosh^2(\sqrt{3}t)dx^2, }
nodes.statement_short: The Nariai metric: a constant round $\mathbb S^2$ factor of curvature $1$ times a $\cosh$-expanding $\mathbb S^1$ factor.

nodes.name: Instability of the Nariai solution
nodes.statement: The Nariai solution is unstable in the class of product manifolds of the type \eqref{ansatz} on $\mathbb S^1\times \mathbb S^2$, i.e.~there are arbitrarily small perturbations with an incomplete MGHD.
nodes.origin_citation: cf. Beyer 2009 (Non-genericity of the Nariai solutions I, II)
assumptions: in the class of product manifolds of the type \eqref{ansatz} on $\mathbb S^1\times \mathbb S^2$
conclusions: there are arbitrarily small perturbations with an incomplete MGHD

nodes.name: Complete analysis of the 3-dimensional space of product initial data
nodes.statement: A complete analysis of the 3-dimensional space of initial data with this product structure with techniques similar to those used in \cite{AnHe07} is clearly desirable.
nodes.statement_short: A full analysis of the whole 3-parameter product initial-data space (beyond one-parameter families) remains to be carried out.

nodes.name: Hawking singularity theorem with positive cosmological constant
nodes.statement: Let $(\overline M^{n+1},\mathbf{g})$ be a $n+1$-dimensional globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold and suppose \eq{Ric(X,X)\geq -n |\mathbf g(X,X)|} for all timelike vectors $X$. Assume furthermore that there exists a hypersurface $M$ whose expansion satisfies $\theta\leq \theta_0<-n$. Then, $(\overline M,\mathbf g)$ is future geodesically incomplete.
nodes.statement_short: A timelike Ricci lower bound plus a hypersurface with expansion $\theta\leq\theta_0<-n$ forces future geodesic incompleteness.

nodes.name: Incompleteness for MGHDs with a negatively curved Cauchy hypersurface
nodes.statement: Let $(\overline{M},\mathbf{g})$ be a MGHD of Einstein's equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}>0$. If $\overline{M}$ contains a Cauchy hypersurface $M$ whose induced metric has scalar curvature $R(g)<R_0<0$, then $\overline{M}$ is geodesically incomplete either to the future or to the past.
nodes.statement_short: A MGHD with $\Lambda=n(n-1)/2$ containing a Cauchy surface of scalar curvature $R(g)<R_0<0$ is geodesically incomplete in one time direction.

nodes.name: Proof of the incompleteness corollary
nodes.statement: Let $g$ be the induced metric on $M$ and as above, let $K$ be the second fundamental form of $M$ and $\Sigma=K-\frac{1}{n}H$ its tracefree part. By the constraint equations, \eq{n(n-1)=R(g)-|K|^2+H^2=R(g)-|\Sigma|^2+\frac{n-1}{n}H^2\leq R_0+ \frac{n-1}{n}H^2,} so that \eq{\theta^2=H^2\geq (n(n-1)-R_0)\frac{n}{n-1}>n^2.} After time reflection, if necessary, we may conclude \eq{\theta\leq \theta_0<-n} and now future incompleteness follows from the above singularity theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the scalar-curvature bound into the Hamiltonian constraint to get $\theta^2>n^2$, then apply the singularity theorem after a time reflection.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: We first prove Case 1. By assumptions on the $\lambda_i$, $y''(0)=n-\lambda_2<0$ and $x''(0)=n-\lambda_1>\frac{n}{n_1}>0$. Then, $x$ is monotonically increasing: If $t_0>0$ is the first time such that $x'(t_0)=0$, we get $x''(t_0)>\frac{n}{n_1}>0$ (if $\lambda_1\leq0$, we even get $x''(t_0)\geq n)$ which implies $x'(t)<0$ for $t\in (t_0-\varepsilon,t_0)$ and thus contradicts the assumption. Analogously, one shows that $y$ is monotonically decreasing. Now we show that as long as $y$ is uniformly bounded, its derivatives exist and $x$ and its derivatives cannot blow up in finite time. If $y'\leq-1$ and $y\geq Y_0$, we obtain by monotonicity, the evolution equation and $x'y'<0$ that \eq{y''\geq -C (y')^2} which after dividing by $y'$ and integration in turn implies \eq{\log|y'|\leq C(1-Y_0),} i.e. $y'$ is bounded. Observe that by the evolution equation, we get $x''\leq n+Cx'$ as long as $y'>-C$ which implies the assertion on $x$. Next we show that $y$ is unbounded. If not, it must converge to a limit by monotonicity, so we have $y(\infty)=\lim_{t\to\infty} y(t)$. Then we get either a sequence of $t_i\to\infty$ such that $y''(t_i)=0$ or $\lim_{t\to\infty} y''(t)=0$. The first case cannot occur, since then $y''(t_i)=n-\lambda_2e^{-2y(t_0)}\geq \frac{n}{n_1}>0$. In the latter case, we necessarily get $\lim x'(t)=\infty$ by the evolution of $y$. On the other hand, by the constraint equation, \eq{n_1x''-n_2y''=n(n_1-n_2)-n_1\lambda_1e^{-2x}+n_2\lambda_2e^{-2y}-n_1^2(x')^2+n_2^2(y')^2\\ \leq C-n_1^2(x')^2+n_2^2(y')^2} From the constraint and adding the evolution equations, we also easily obtain \eq{n_1(x''+(x')^2)+n_2(y''+(y')^2)=n,} from which we get \eq{-n_1(x')^2-2n_2y''+n-n_2(y')^2\leq C-n_1^2(x')^2+n_2^2(y')^2} and therefore, since $n_1>1$ (if $n_1=1$, the above bound implies $\lambda_1<0$ which in turn contradicts $n_1=1$), we get a bound on $x'$ if $y'$ and $y''$ are bounded. This yields the contradiction. By monotonicity of $x$ and $y$ and the unboundedness of $y$ from below there is a constant $C>0$ and a time $t_1>0$ such that the differential inequality \eq{ n_1x''+n_2y''\leq-C-(n_1x'+n_2y')^2 } holds for all $t\geq t_1$. By ODE comparison, $z(t)=n_1x'(t)+n_2y'(t)\leq -\sqrt{C}\tan(D+\sqrt{C}(t-t_1))$ for $t\geq t_1$ and some $D\in\R$. Therefore, $z\to-\infty$ as $t$ approaches some $t_+$. As $x'>0$, $y'\to-\infty$. We also have $y(t)\leq\frac{1}{n_2}\int_0^{t}z(s)ds\to-\infty$ as $t\to t_+$, which implies that $y$ diverges. In addition, because \eq{x''=n-\lambda_1e^{-2x}-zx'\geq -zx',} we obtain $x(t)\geq \int_0^t\exp(-\int_0^sz(r)dr)ds\to \infty$ as $t\to t_+$. It remains to show that the Kretschmann scalar is unbounded at the singularity: Let $0$ be the index referring to the $t$-coordinate and $i,j$ and $a,b$ be indices referring to coordinates on $M_1,M_2$ respectively. One can check that the coefficients with an odd number of zeros vanish and therefore, the Kretschmann scalar satisfies \eq{ |\tilde{R}|^2=\tilde{R}_{\mu\nu\lambda\sigma}\tilde{R}^{\mu\nu\lambda\sigma}\geq 0} because all summands are nonnegative. Now it can be checked that \eq{ \tilde{R}_{0ij0}=-\frac{\partial^2_t a}{a} \tilde{g}_{ij},\qquad \tilde{R}_{0ab0}=-\frac{\partial^2_t b}{b} \tilde{g}_{ab},} so that \eq{|\tilde{R}|^2\geq \left(n_1\frac{\partial^2_t a}{a}\right)^2+n_2\left(\frac{\partial^2_t b}{b}\right)^2=n_1(x''+(x')^2)^2+n_2(y''+(y')^2)^2} where as above $x=\log(a)$, $y=\log(b)$. Now, since $x\to\infty$ as $t\to t_+$, we also get $x''+(x')^2\to\infty$, which shows that the Kretschmann scalar must blow up. This finishes the proof in Case 1. In Case 2, it is easy to see that the metric given in the statement of the theorem is the MGHD of the given initial data. Let us now consider Case 3. By assumption, \eq{ y''(0)=n-\lambda_2\in(0,1) } and \eq{ x''(0)=n-\lambda_1\in (1,\frac{n}{n_1}). } Both $x$ and $y$ are strictly monotonically increasing. We have $x'(t)>0$ for small $t$. Let $t_0$ be the first time, where $x'(t_0)=0$. Then we obtain \eq{ x''(t_0)=n-\lambda_1e^{-2x(t_0)}>0, } as long as $y'(t_0)$ exists. Thus $x'<0$ on $(t_0-\varepsilon,t_0)$, which causes the contradiction. Analogously one shows that $y$ is strictly monotonically increasing. From the evolution equations and monotonicity we deduce \eq{ n^2-n_1\lambda_1-n_2\lambda_2-(n_1x'+n_2y')^2\leq n_1x''+n_2y''\leq n^2-(n_1x'+n_2y')^2. } The solution of the corresponding ODE, $z'=n^2-z^2$, is $z(t)=n\tanh(nt+c)$, where $c\in \R$. By the initial conditions this implies $0<n_1x'+n_2y'<n$ for all $t>0$. Due to the positivity of $x'$ and $y'$ these statements hold for $x'$ and $y'$ individually. In particular, $x$ and $y$ exist for all times, which finishes the proof of Case 3. Finally, recollapse of MGHDs of small perturbations of the initial data induced by the models follows by the Cauchy stability of the Einstein equations in combination with Theorem \ref{sing-thm}. As the background solutions have Cauchy surfaces of strictly positive and strictly negative mean curvature, this also holds for the MGHDs of small perturbations. Then the singularity theorem yields incompleteness. This idea of proof is explained in further detail originally in \cite{Ri09}. Stability in the expanding direction follows from the results in \cite{Ri08}.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis: monotonicity of $x,y$ by contradiction and ODE comparison give finite-time blow-up in Case 1, the explicit metric settles Case 2, global bounds settle Case 3, and Cauchy stability plus the singularity theorem give the stability statements.

nodes.name: Case 1: monotonicity of $x$ and $y$
nodes.statement: We first prove Case 1. By assumptions on the $\lambda_i$, $y''(0)=n-\lambda_2<0$ and $x''(0)=n-\lambda_1>\frac{n}{n_1}>0$. Then, $x$ is monotonically increasing: If $t_0>0$ is the first time such that $x'(t_0)=0$, we get $x''(t_0)>\frac{n}{n_1}>0$ (if $\lambda_1\leq0$, we even get $x''(t_0)\geq n)$ which implies $x'(t)<0$ for $t\in (t_0-\varepsilon,t_0)$ and thus contradicts the assumption. Analogously, one shows that $y$ is monotonically decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Show $x$ is monotonically increasing and $y$ monotonically decreasing, by contradiction at a first critical time.

nodes.name: No finite-time blow-up while $y$ is bounded
nodes.statement: Now we show that as long as $y$ is uniformly bounded, its derivatives exist and $x$ and its derivatives cannot blow up in finite time. If $y'\leq-1$ and $y\geq Y_0$, we obtain by monotonicity, the evolution equation and $x'y'<0$ that \eq{y''\geq -C (y')^2} which after dividing by $y'$ and integration in turn implies \eq{\log|y'|\leq C(1-Y_0),} i.e. $y'$ is bounded. Observe that by the evolution equation, we get $x''\leq n+Cx'$ as long as $y'>-C$ which implies the assertion on $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $y'$ via $y''\geq -C(y')^2$ and then $x$ via $x''\leq n+Cx'$.

nodes.name: Unboundedness of $y$
nodes.statement: Next we show that $y$ is unbounded. If not, it must converge to a limit by monotonicity, so we have $y(\infty)=\lim_{t\to\infty} y(t)$. Then we get either a sequence of $t_i\to\infty$ such that $y''(t_i)=0$ or $\lim_{t\to\infty} y''(t)=0$. The first case cannot occur, since then $y''(t_i)=n-\lambda_2e^{-2y(t_0)}\geq \frac{n}{n_1}>0$. In the latter case, we necessarily get $\lim x'(t)=\infty$ by the evolution of $y$. On the other hand, by the constraint equation, \eq{n_1x''-n_2y''=n(n_1-n_2)-n_1\lambda_1e^{-2x}+n_2\lambda_2e^{-2y}-n_1^2(x')^2+n_2^2(y')^2\\ \leq C-n_1^2(x')^2+n_2^2(y')^2} From the constraint and adding the evolution equations, we also easily obtain \eq{n_1(x''+(x')^2)+n_2(y''+(y')^2)=n,} from which we get \eq{-n_1(x')^2-2n_2y''+n-n_2(y')^2\leq C-n_1^2(x')^2+n_2^2(y')^2} and therefore, since $n_1>1$ (if $n_1=1$, the above bound implies $\lambda_1<0$ which in turn contradicts $n_1=1$), we get a bound on $x'$ if $y'$ and $y''$ are bounded. This yields the contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $y$ converges and derive a contradiction from the constraint and evolution equations.

nodes.name: Finite-time blow-up by ODE comparison
nodes.statement: By monotonicity of $x$ and $y$ and the unboundedness of $y$ from below there is a constant $C>0$ and a time $t_1>0$ such that the differential inequality \eq{ n_1x''+n_2y''\leq-C-(n_1x'+n_2y')^2 } holds for all $t\geq t_1$. By ODE comparison, $z(t)=n_1x'(t)+n_2y'(t)\leq -\sqrt{C}\tan(D+\sqrt{C}(t-t_1))$ for $t\geq t_1$ and some $D\in\R$. Therefore, $z\to-\infty$ as $t$ approaches some $t_+$. As $x'>0$, $y'\to-\infty$. We also have $y(t)\leq\frac{1}{n_2}\int_0^{t}z(s)ds\to-\infty$ as $t\to t_+$, which implies that $y$ diverges. In addition, because \eq{x''=n-\lambda_1e^{-2x}-zx'\geq -zx',} we obtain $x(t)\geq \int_0^t\exp(-\int_0^sz(r)dr)ds\to \infty$ as $t\to t_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare with $z'\leq -C-z^2$ to get $z\to-\infty$ at a finite $t_+$, with $y\to-\infty$ and $x\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Blow-up of the Kretschmann scalar
nodes.statement: It remains to show that the Kretschmann scalar is unbounded at the singularity: Let $0$ be the index referring to the $t$-coordinate and $i,j$ and $a,b$ be indices referring to coordinates on $M_1,M_2$ respectively. One can check that the coefficients with an odd number of zeros vanish and therefore, the Kretschmann scalar satisfies \eq{ |\tilde{R}|^2=\tilde{R}_{\mu\nu\lambda\sigma}\tilde{R}^{\mu\nu\lambda\sigma}\geq 0} because all summands are nonnegative. Now it can be checked that \eq{ \tilde{R}_{0ij0}=-\frac{\partial^2_t a}{a} \tilde{g}_{ij},\qquad \tilde{R}_{0ab0}=-\frac{\partial^2_t b}{b} \tilde{g}_{ab},} so that \eq{|\tilde{R}|^2\geq \left(n_1\frac{\partial^2_t a}{a}\right)^2+n_2\left(\frac{\partial^2_t b}{b}\right)^2=n_1(x''+(x')^2)^2+n_2(y''+(y')^2)^2} where as above $x=\log(a)$, $y=\log(b)$. Now, since $x\to\infty$ as $t\to t_+$, we also get $x''+(x')^2\to\infty$, which shows that the Kretschmann scalar must blow up. This finishes the proof in Case 1.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|\tilde R|^2$ from below by $n_1(x''+(x')^2)^2+n_2(y''+(y')^2)^2$, which diverges.

nodes.name: Case 2: the explicit critical solution
nodes.statement: In Case 2, it is easy to see that the metric given in the statement of the theorem is the MGHD of the given initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the explicit metric of the theorem as the MGHD in the critical case.

nodes.name: Case 3: global existence via monotonicity and ODE comparison
nodes.statement: Let us now consider Case 3. By assumption, \eq{ y''(0)=n-\lambda_2\in(0,1) } and \eq{ x''(0)=n-\lambda_1\in (1,\frac{n}{n_1}). } Both $x$ and $y$ are strictly monotonically increasing. We have $x'(t)>0$ for small $t$. Let $t_0$ be the first time, where $x'(t_0)=0$. Then we obtain \eq{ x''(t_0)=n-\lambda_1e^{-2x(t_0)}>0, } as long as $y'(t_0)$ exists. Thus $x'<0$ on $(t_0-\varepsilon,t_0)$, which causes the contradiction. Analogously one shows that $y$ is strictly monotonically increasing. From the evolution equations and monotonicity we deduce \eq{ n^2-n_1\lambda_1-n_2\lambda_2-(n_1x'+n_2y')^2\leq n_1x''+n_2y''\leq n^2-(n_1x'+n_2y')^2. } The solution of the corresponding ODE, $z'=n^2-z^2$, is $z(t)=n\tanh(nt+c)$, where $c\in \R$. By the initial conditions this implies $0<n_1x'+n_2y'<n$ for all $t>0$. Due to the positivity of $x'$ and $y'$ these statements hold for $x'$ and $y'$ individually. In particular, $x$ and $y$ exist for all times, which finishes the proof of Case 3.
nodes.statement_short: Show $x,y$ strictly increase and $0<n_1x'+n_2y'<n$ via the comparison ODE $z'=n^2-z^2$, giving global existence.

nodes.name: Stability of the behavior under perturbation of initial data
nodes.statement: Finally, recollapse of MGHDs of small perturbations of the initial data induced by the models follows by the Cauchy stability of the Einstein equations in combination with Theorem \ref{sing-thm}. As the background solutions have Cauchy surfaces of strictly positive and strictly negative mean curvature, this also holds for the MGHDs of small perturbations. Then the singularity theorem yields incompleteness. This idea of proof is explained in further detail originally in \cite{Ri09}. Stability in the expanding direction follows from the results in \cite{Ri08}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Cauchy stability with the singularity theorem for recollapse, and cite Ringström for the expanding direction.

nodes.name: Expansion rate of the warping factors in Case 3
nodes.statement: With some more effort, we can determine the expansion rate of the warping factors of the solutions appearing in Case 3: By the above, we have $n_1x'(t)+n_2y'(t)>C_1>0$ for all $t\geq t_1$ and $n_1x(t)+n_2y(t)>C_2t$ for all $t\geq t_1$ and $C_2>0$. Using this, we can improve the above estimate. Denoting $z=n_1x'+n_2y'$ as above, we get \eq{ n^2-Ce^{-Ct}-z^2\leq z'\leq n^2-z^2. } from which we obtain the uniform bounds $0\geq z-n\geq -Ce^{-Ct}$. After integrating, \eq{0\geq n_1x+n_2y-nt\geq -C.} Similarly, we obtain for $w:=n_1x'-n_2y'$ the estimate \eq{ n(n_1-n_2)-Ce^{-C t} -zw \leq w'\leq n(n_1-n_2)+Ce^{-C t} -zw} which implies because of the estimate on $n-z$ that $|w-(n_1-n_2)|\leq Ce^{-Ct}$. Again by integrating, \eq{{C_1\geq n_1x-n_2y-(n_1-n_2)t\geq C_2.}} Finally, we obtain from \eqref{z} and \eqref{w} that $\sup \left\{|x-t|,|y-t|\right\}\leq C$. It is immediate that the warping functions satisfy $C_1 e^t\leq a(t) \leq C_2e^t$ and $C_1 e^t\leq b(t) \leq C_2e^t$ for $t\geq0$.
nodes.statement_short: Refined estimates give $\sup\{|x-t|,|y-t|\}\leq C$, hence both warping functions grow like $e^t$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\leq 0$, we are going to show that all corresponding solutions are geodesically incomplete in one direction and geodesically complete in the other. Let us first remark that the case where $R(g)\equiv |\Sigma|\equiv 0$ corresponds to the solution $-dt^2+e^{2t}g$ which is geodesically incomplete in the past and geodesically complete in the future. Therefore we assume $R(g)-|\Sigma|^2\leq R_0<0$ from now on. By the constraint equation, we have \eq{n(n-1)=R(g)-|K|^2+H^2=R(g)-|\Sigma|^2+\frac{n-1}{n}H^2\leq R_0+ \frac{n-1}{n}H^2,} As above, we get $|\theta|\geq \theta_0>n$. If $\theta\leq-\theta_0<-n$, we obtain geodesic incompleteness by Proposition \ref{sing-thm}. If $\theta\geq\theta_0>n$, we have the differential inequality \eq{ \partial_t \theta\leq n-\frac{1}{n}\theta^2} so that we have the upper bound \eq{\theta \leq n\cdot\frac{e^{2t}-A_0}{e^{2t}+A_0}= \frac{n}{1-|A_0|e^{-2t}}(1+|A_0|e^{-2t})\leq n+n|A_0|e^{-2t}} where $A_0=\frac{n-\theta_0}{n+\theta_0}$. Again by the constraint equation, \eq{0\leq-R(g)+|\Sigma|^2= \frac{n-1}{n}(\theta^2-n^2)\leq Ce^{-2t}. } In particular, since $R(g)=n_1\lambda_1e^{-2x}+n_2\lambda_2 e^{-2y}$, both factors $x,y$ grow linearly, in particular, they do not converge to $-\infty$. Thus, they are geodesically complete.
nodes.statement_short: Split on the sign of the expansion $\theta$: one sign gives incompleteness by the singularity theorem, the other gives $\theta\to n$ exponentially and hence completeness.

nodes.name: Statement of what is to be shown
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\leq 0$, we are going to show that all corresponding solutions are geodesically incomplete in one direction and geodesically complete in the other.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the goal: incompleteness in one time direction, completeness in the other.

nodes.name: Dispose of the flat case and fix the standing assumption
nodes.statement: Let us first remark that the case where $R(g)\equiv |\Sigma|\equiv 0$ corresponds to the solution $-dt^2+e^{2t}g$ which is geodesically incomplete in the past and geodesically complete in the future. Therefore we assume $R(g)-|\Sigma|^2\leq R_0<0$ from now on.
nodes.statement_short: Handle $R(g)\equiv|\Sigma|\equiv 0$ separately and assume $R(g)-|\Sigma|^2\leq R_0<0$ afterwards.

nodes.name: Expansion bound from the constraint equation
nodes.statement: By the constraint equation, we have \eq{n(n-1)=R(g)-|K|^2+H^2=R(g)-|\Sigma|^2+\frac{n-1}{n}H^2\leq R_0+ \frac{n-1}{n}H^2,} As above, we get $|\theta|\geq \theta_0>n$.
nodes.statement_short: The constraint gives $|\theta|\geq\theta_0>n$.

nodes.name: Negative expansion: incompleteness
nodes.statement: If $\theta\leq-\theta_0<-n$, we obtain geodesic incompleteness by Proposition \ref{sing-thm}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the singularity theorem in the contracting case.

nodes.name: Positive expansion: upper bound on $\theta$
nodes.statement: If $\theta\geq\theta_0>n$, we have the differential inequality \eq{ \partial_t \theta\leq n-\frac{1}{n}\theta^2} so that we have the upper bound \eq{\theta \leq n\cdot\frac{e^{2t}-A_0}{e^{2t}+A_0}= \frac{n}{1-|A_0|e^{-2t}}(1+|A_0|e^{-2t})\leq n+n|A_0|e^{-2t}} where $A_0=\frac{n-\theta_0}{n+\theta_0}$.
nodes.statement_short: From $\partial_t\theta\leq n-\frac{1}{n}\theta^2$ derive $\theta\leq n+n|A_0|e^{-2t}$.

nodes.name: Linear growth of both factors and completeness
nodes.statement: Again by the constraint equation, \eq{0\leq-R(g)+|\Sigma|^2= \frac{n-1}{n}(\theta^2-n^2)\leq Ce^{-2t}. } In particular, since $R(g)=n_1\lambda_1e^{-2x}+n_2\lambda_2 e^{-2y}$, both factors $x,y$ grow linearly, in particular, they do not converge to $-\infty$. Thus, they are geodesically complete.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential decay of $-R(g)+|\Sigma|^2$ forces linear growth of $x,y$, hence completeness.

nodes.name: Exponential convergence of the expansion in the complete direction
nodes.statement: Since $\theta\to n$ and $ |\Sigma|^2\to 0$ exponentially, one concludes that $x',y'\to 1$ exponentially and $\sup \left\{|x-t|,|y-t|\right\}\leq C$ as in Remark \ref{expansionrate}.

nodes.name: Expected Kasner-type singularity in the incomplete direction
nodes.statement: We expect that the generic type of singularity that occurs in the geodesically incomplete direction is of Kasner type, i.e. one of the factors goes to $\infty$ while the other goes to $-\infty$ as $t\to t_+$. This also implies a blow-up of the Kretschmann scalar as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm-1}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement: We have the data $n_1=2$, $n_2=1$, $\lambda_1=\lambda$, $\lambda_2=0$, so the evolution equations are \eq{\alg{x''&=3-\lambda e^{-2x}-2(x')^2-x'y'\\ y''&=3-(y')^2-2x'y'}} and the constraint equation reduce to \eq{6=2\lambda e^{-2x}+2(x')^2+4x'y'.} We demand $y'(0)=0$ such that we obtain a one-parameter family of solutions by prescribing $\lambda$ and $x'(0)$ such that \eq{3=\lambda+(x'(0))^2} by the constraint. Recall that we generally require $x(0)=0$. For our purposes, we additionally assume $\lambda>0$ throughout. By using the constraint, the equation on $x$ decouples as \eq{\alg{x''&=3-\lambda e^{-2x}-2(x')^2-x'y'=\frac{1}{2}(3-\lambda e^{-2x}-3(x')^2).}} Now we show that the MGHD is future incomplete, if $\lambda<3$ and $x'(0)<0$. At first, \eq{x''(0)=3-\lambda-2x'(0)^2=(3-\lambda-(x'(0))^2)-x'(0)^2<0,} which shows that both $x$ and $x'$ are monotonically decreasing for small time. In addition, as long as $x$ and $x'$ are monotonically decreasing, we have \eq{x''=\frac{1}{2}(3-\lambda e^{-2x}-3(x')^2)\leq\frac{1}{2}(3-\lambda-2(x'(0)))\leq \frac{1}{2}x''(0)<0,} which shows that this monotonicity property holds for all time and $x$ and $x'$ are unbounded. In particular, for large time, we get \eq{x''\leq -\frac{3}{2}(x')^2. } This shows that $x'\to -\infty$ as $t$ approaches some $t_+$, since the comparison ODE is solved by $z(t)=\frac{2}{c+3t}$. By integrating, one obtains the estimate \eq{x(t)\leq C_1+\log(C_2-\frac{3}{2}t)} for some constants $C_1,C_2>0$ which shows that also $x\to-\infty$ as $t\to t_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize to $n_1=2$, $n_2=1$, decouple the $x$-equation with the constraint, and show $x''\leq-\frac{3}{2}(x')^2$ drives $x\to-\infty$ at a finite $t_+$.

nodes.name: Specialize the evolution and constraint equations to $\mathbb S^1\times\mathbb S^2$
nodes.statement: We have the data $n_1=2$, $n_2=1$, $\lambda_1=\lambda$, $\lambda_2=0$, so the evolution equations are \eq{\alg{x''&=3-\lambda e^{-2x}-2(x')^2-x'y'\\ y''&=3-(y')^2-2x'y'}} and the constraint equation reduce to \eq{6=2\lambda e^{-2x}+2(x')^2+4x'y'.}
nodes.statement_short: Insert $n_1=2$, $n_2=1$, $\lambda_2=0$ into the ODE system and the constraint.

nodes.name: Prescribe the one-parameter family of initial data
nodes.statement: We demand $y'(0)=0$ such that we obtain a one-parameter family of solutions by prescribing $\lambda$ and $x'(0)$ such that \eq{3=\lambda+(x'(0))^2} by the constraint. Recall that we generally require $x(0)=0$. For our purposes, we additionally assume $\lambda>0$ throughout.

nodes.name: Decouple the equation for $x$
nodes.statement: By using the constraint, the equation on $x$ decouples as \eq{\alg{x''&=3-\lambda e^{-2x}-2(x')^2-x'y'=\frac{1}{2}(3-\lambda e^{-2x}-3(x')^2).}}
nodes.statement_short: Use the constraint to rewrite $x''=\frac{1}{2}(3-\lambda e^{-2x}-3(x')^2)$.

nodes.name: Initial decrease of $x$ and $x'$
nodes.statement: Now we show that the MGHD is future incomplete, if $\lambda<3$ and $x'(0)<0$. At first, \eq{x''(0)=3-\lambda-2x'(0)^2=(3-\lambda-(x'(0))^2)-x'(0)^2<0,} which shows that both $x$ and $x'$ are monotonically decreasing for small time.
nodes.statement_short: For $\lambda<3$ and $x'(0)<0$ show $x''(0)<0$, so $x$ and $x'$ initially decrease.

nodes.name: Monotonicity persists and yields $x''\leq-\frac{3}{2}(x')^2$
nodes.statement: In addition, as long as $x$ and $x'$ are monotonically decreasing, we have \eq{x''=\frac{1}{2}(3-\lambda e^{-2x}-3(x')^2)\leq\frac{1}{2}(3-\lambda-2(x'(0)))\leq \frac{1}{2}x''(0)<0,} which shows that this monotonicity property holds for all time and $x$ and $x'$ are unbounded. In particular, for large time, we get \eq{x''\leq -\frac{3}{2}(x')^2. }
nodes.statement_short: Bootstrap the monotonicity to all times and extract the differential inequality for large time.

nodes.name: Finite-time blow-up of $x'$ and divergence of $x$
nodes.statement: This shows that $x'\to -\infty$ as $t$ approaches some $t_+$, since the comparison ODE is solved by $z(t)=\frac{2}{c+3t}$. By integrating, one obtains the estimate \eq{x(t)\leq C_1+\log(C_2-\frac{3}{2}t)} for some constants $C_1,C_2>0$ which shows that also $x\to-\infty$ as $t\to t_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare with $z(t)=\frac{2}{c+3t}$ and integrate to get $x\to-\infty$ at a finite $t_+$.

nodes.name: The singularity of the perturbed Nariai solution is of Kasner type
nodes.statement: We are also able to show that this singularity is of Kasner type, i.e. $y(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to t_+$. At first note that $y$ is monotonically increasing for small time. In fact, it is monotonically increasing for all $t>0$ since $y''(t_0)=3>0$ as long as $y'(t_0)=0$. But then we have an estimate \eq{y'' \geq 3-(y')^2+2 |z|y'} and since $z\to\infty$ as $t\to t_+$ this shows that $y'\to\infty$ as $t\to t_+$ and because the integral of $z$ diverges, we get that also $y$ diverges as $t\to t_+$.
nodes.statement_short: The second factor satisfies $y(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to t_+$, so the singularity is Kasner-like.

nodes.name: Completeness in the opposite time direction for the Nariai perturbations
nodes.statement: A similar analysis as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm-1} shows that every MGHD is complete in the other time-direction and arguments as in Remark \ref{expansionrate} imply exponential growth of both warping functions in the past.
